- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is falling, model underestimates the decline; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag 1–2 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight downward bias if sentiment is weak.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
